text:
Sean Gallagher: trying to close the loop on rollback automation for profile pack defaults. need crisp answers on: (1) who can trigger (2) what exactly gets reverted (profile_version vs individual knobs) (3) audit trail. can we finalize today so i can update the on-call runbook?

Rafael Mendes: yep. current proposal from canary playbook: one button in rollout-service + CLI for breakglass. rollback action = revert `runtime.profile_version_default` for cohort + set `profile_pack_enabled=false` if needed.

Omar El-Sayed: +1 on reverting version vs knobs. rolling back individual knobs is basically “recreate the old profile” and we’ll drift. version rollback is deterministic.

Ethan Park: control plane side we can do both but would prefer one “atomic” patch:
- cohort config: `profile_version_pin` (nullable)
- global default: `profile_version_default`
- feature flag: `enable_profile_pack`

Benji Okafor: guardrails question: do we allow rollback to *any* previous version or only last-known-good (LKG) for that SKU?

Rafael Mendes: my take: allow any installed version *that passes compatibility check* + only within same runtime major (1.22.x). for hosted emergency, we basically always rollback to LKG though.

Neha Kapoor: can we be explicit: rollback automation should only offer “LKG per SKU per region” in UI. CLI can accept explicit version but requires reason + ticket link.

Sean Gallagher: +1. we got burned last time with “pick any”. UI should bias safe.

Connor O'Brien: release eng POV: we should define LKG as “last version that passed perf-canary gates + ran for >=24h on canary w/o SLO violation”. we can publish LKG in release notes.

Allison Grant: audit trail: i need structured fields so dashboards can show “who changed profile defaults” + correlate to latency shifts. can we emit an event w/ version_from/version_to + cohort + sku labels?

Ethan Park: yep. rollout-service already emits an audit event but it’s currently free-form. i can add typed fields:
`actor`, `actor_role`, `request_id`, `reason`, `env`, `region`, `cohort`, `sku`, `from_version`, `to_version`, `kill_switch_toggled`, `diff_summary`.

Benji Okafor: who qualifies as actor_role? we should codify permissions.

Sean Gallagher: proposed permissioning:
- SRE on-call (primary/secondary) can trigger rollback in Hosted.
- Runtime on-call can trigger too (same perms) for off-hours.
- Release captain can trigger during release window.
- Everyone else: read-only.

Paula Mendes: for Dedicated, need a different rule. product wants Dedicated changes opt-in + we shouldn’t flip customer pins without explicit approval.

Omar El-Sayed: agree. rollback automation in Dedicated should revert *fleet default* but must not touch customer `profile_version_pin` overrides.

Rafael Mendes: so: Hosted rollback affects cohort defaults + (optionally) kill-switch for pack.
Dedicated rollback affects pool defaults only (no per-customer pins).
Private: no automation, just docs/helm values.

Mateo Alvarez: +1. also: define what “kill-switch” does precisely. i want it to force runtime to ignore profile pack selection and fall back to legacy defaults (pre-1.22), not just “stop updating”.

Ethan Park: implemented semantics (PR in flight):
- `enable_profile_pack=false` => runtime uses legacy config path and logs `profile_pack_disabled_reason=control_plane`.
- still reports detected sku, but `profile_id=legacy-default`.

Sean Gallagher: perfect. now the “what gets reverted” section:
Option A: revert `profile_version_default` only.
Option B: revert version + clear any cohort-level knob overrides.

Benji Okafor: if we keep knob overrides at all, they need to be treated as “hotfix overrides” w/ TTL. i’d prefer rollback clears them.

Omar El-Sayed: +1 clear overrides. if we rollback because p99 exploded, leaving an override from the bad version around defeats the purpose.

Paula Mendes: careful: some overrides are stabilizers (ex: L40S headroom) that we might want to keep while rolling back version.

Neha Kapoor: can we classify overrides into:
- “temporary hotfix” (auto-cleared on rollback)
- “safety caps” (persist)

Ethan Park: technically yes but adds complexity + policy. i’d rather keep it simple for v1.

Rafael Mendes: pragmatic v1:
- rollback action does: set `profile_version_default = LKG`, and set `override_bundle_id = null` for the target cohort.
- if we need safety caps, we encode them into the LKG profile definition.

Allison Grant: +1. easier to debug. override_bundle_id=null is auditable.

Paula Mendes: ok, but then we need a playbook step to confirm the LKG profile includes the safety cap we care about (esp L40S OOM).

Sean Gallagher: that’s fine. runbook can say “if rollback is for OOM, prefer kill-switch OR rollback to LKG that includes headroom fix; verify on dashboard X”.

Connor O'Brien: release note will call out which versions include which safety cap. we can link to expected behavior docs.

Benji Okafor: break-glass: do we require approvals for CLI rollback to non-LKG?

Neha Kapoor: yes. requirement:
- Hosted: non-LKG rollback requires approval from SRE on-call + runtime on-call (two-person).
- Additionally if it’s cross-major (should be blocked), require Neha+Mateo (but ideally hard-block).

Ethan Park: we can enforce:
- UI only allows LKG.
- CLI allows explicit `--to-version`, but if `--to-version != lkg` then require `--approver` fields (two emails) and it pings Slack for ack before applying.

Rafael Mendes: can we keep it less heavy? approvals via Slack interactions are flaky during incidents.

Sean Gallagher: agree. for incident path, i’d rather:
- hard-block cross-major.
- allow non-LKG within same minor but require a ticket link + emits HIGH severity audit event + auto-post in #incidents + #eng-sre.
- SRE on-call owns it.

Neha Kapoor: ok. i can live with that. no interactive approvals.

SREBot: Reminder: changes to rollout automation require runbook update + pager exercise. Please link the final doc in ENG-SRE runbooks.

Allison Grant: audit trail destinations:
1) AuditLog (structured)
2) Slack notification in #eng-sre (always)
3) Slack notification in #incidents if `kill_switch_toggled=true` OR `p99_gate_breached=true` OR non-LKG

Ethan Park: done. i’ll add a webhook from rollout-service to slack notifier w/ template:
“ROLLBACK: env=hosted region=us-east cohort=hosted-canary sku=H100 from=1.22.0-ppack.3 to=1.22.0-ppack.2 actor=sean.g reason=… request_id=…”

Omar El-Sayed: also include `estimated_impact` field? like % traffic in cohort.

Rafael Mendes: we have cohort size. can include `traffic_share=2%`.

Sean Gallagher: final decisions (plz react/confirm):
- Who can trigger: SRE on-call + Runtime on-call + Release captain (Hosted). Dedicated: SRE + Release captain for pool defaults only.
- What is reverted: `profile_version_default` to LKG + clear `override_bundle_id` for that cohort/pool. Optional: toggle kill-switch `enable_profile_pack=false`.
- What is NOT touched: per-customer `profile_version_pin` (Dedicated), Private installs.
- Audit trail: structured audit event + slack posts; include actor, request_id, from/to version, cohort/pool, sku/region, diff summary, traffic share.

Neha Kapoor: :thumbsup: confirm.

Mateo Alvarez: :thumbsup: confirm. + please make sure runtime logs the transition clearly at startup (active profile + “why”).

Connor O'Brien: :thumbsup: confirm. i’ll add LKG definition to release checklist.

Paula Mendes: :thumbsup: ok.

Allison Grant: :thumbsup: confirm. send me the final field names so i can wire dashboards.

Ethan Park: ack. i’ll post the schema in the PR description + drop it here when merged.

Rafael Mendes: once Ethan’s PR lands i’ll update the rollout checklist doc w/ exact commands.

Sean Gallagher: thanks all. i’ll update the on-call runbook + schedule a quick game day for “rollback to LKG” next week.
